fatalFlaws: Block-size dependent smoothing cadence in the loop. `if (i % kCtrlInterval == 0) refreshLoopCoeffs()` restarts the 16-sample cadence at every block boundary, and refreshLoopCoeffs advances the smoothers with `fc = clamp(cutoffSmooth.skip(16), 20, 0.45 * sr)`, `res = resSmooth.skip(16)`, `A = absorbSmooth.skip(16)`, `decayGain = decaySmooth.skip(16)`. JUCE's skip(16) advances 16 steps unconditionally, so at block size 1 the condition is true every sample and every loop smoother runs 16x too fast (a 30 ms Decay/Filter ramp becomes 1.9 ms); block 8 is 2x, block 17 is 1.9x, only multiples of 16 are correct. The ChipClock two lines above already does this right with a persistent `ctrlCountdown` member; the loop must use the same persistent countdown (D2's `controlCountdown` member) and never `i %`. Violates 'Make no assumptions about block size' in a place that is audible.

No first-block snap of the clock smoother. `logFsSmooth` is a Linear SmoothedValue (default current = 0), `prepare` is 'recompute host-rate coefficients, then reset()' and 'reset keeps Time, zeroes phase'; verified in juce_SmoothedValue.h that `reset (sr, ramp)` snaps current to the PREVIOUS target, which is 0 after construction. The first process() therefore ramps logFs linearly from 0 to the knob over 20 ms: exp(0) clamps to FS_CHIP_HARD_MIN = 750 Hz for the first ~11 ms (ratio 0.016, about 8 aliased words written per stage), then glides 750 Hz to 177 kHz over the remaining ~9 ms. Those words come back one stage delay later time-compressed ~236x (a 45 us click) on every plugin insert and session load, and every EngineTest scenario starts with 20 ms of pitch glide. Apply the template's `firstBlock` idiom (`setCurrentAndTargetValue` after prepare) plus D2's `snapTimeOnNextBlock()` for preset loads.

Unbounded phase accumulator. `phaseBefore = phase; phase += ratio` with `double phase` never wrapped, and `f.readFrac = frac(phase)`, `f.nTicks = floor(phase) - floor(phaseBefore)` computed on the growing value. readFrac resolution degrades with elapsed time (about 1e-7 chip sample after an hour at ratio 4, 1e-3 after a year of continuous play). Inaudible within a session, but an unbounded accumulator in a real-time loop is a defect on principle and costs one subtraction to remove: D1's `p -= ticks` keeps it in [0,1), after which readFrac is simply the phase.
scores.notes: Winner by half a point, and only because its defects are cadence and initialisation slips inside an otherwise well-bounded structure. Real-time strengths verified: ONE shared `ChipClock::Frame` per host sample feeds all three stages (one exp, one division, computed once); `t = (tickOffset + j) * invRatio` is correct including the frac = 0 edge; the read `dacPrev + readFrac * (dacCur - dacPrev)` is causal with one chip tick of latency; the error-feedback quantizer is provably bounded (|qErr| <= 1.5 LSB given chipClip and the +-1 clamp, and the clamp branch only shrinks |qErr|); `step`/`invStep` are recomputed as a pair at control rate; chip memory is std::array in chip samples so the delay is sample-rate independent by construction; `prepare` chunks oversize blocks; the per-block `isfinite(fb)` flush is a real backstop. The chip-rate DAC pole is the single most important robustness feature in any of the three designs for my lens: it attenuates chip-rate quantisation noise above 8 kHz BEFORE the read decimates 200 kHz to the host rate, which is what makes the short-Time noise floor sample-rate invariant (D1 and D2 discard raw and drift 4 to 6 dB between 48 and 192 kHz). `noiseSrScale = sqrt(sr/48000)` is the correct direction. Defects beyond the fatal list: (a) the cost accounting is false twice: 'Each tick is ~25 flops with no divisions or transcendentals (Pade tanh, ...)' but `fastTanh` is `x * (27 + x*x) / (27 + 9*x*x)`, a division per tick (up to 6 to 7 ticks x 3 stages at 44.1 kHz with FS_CHIP_HARD_MAX 250 kHz, the design says '0..5' which is the soft-max figure), and 'f.invRatio = 1 / ratio // the only division per sample' is contradicted by `lowpass(x): h = 1 / (1 + g*(g + k))` recomputed on every call in three inSvf + three recSvf + three outSvf + loopFilter = 10 more; total is about 30 divisions per host sample worst case, roughly 0.5 % of a core, harmless, but cache h in setG/setK and fix the comments. (b) `(ax - CLIP_KNEE) / (1 - CLIP_KNEE)` is a constant denominator; make it a multiply. (c) The NaN backstop is per block only, so a NaN arriving at sample 0 of a 4096 block emits 4096 NaN samples to the host before the flush; D1's per-sample input sanitiser must sit in front of it. (d) No `ScopedNoDenormals` in the engine; the processor has it but EngineTest has no processor, so every decaying one-pole/SVF state in the harness runs into denormals at silence. (e) `uiLoopEnergy.store(sqrt(energy / n))` is per-sample |y| at block 1 and 85 ms RMS at 4096: the ember's look depends on the host buffer; D2's peak with 50 ms release does not. (f) CLEAR_FADE_SEC 0.003 is short for a -4 dBFS runaway; the `clear` criterion 'max sample-to-sample |difference| <= 0.05' is frequency dependent (a 0.63 peak sine at 1 kHz has a natural step of 0.082). (g) Hiss is injected before the tracking recSvf, so at Time 1 the 'hiss' is a sub-700 Hz rumble. (h) Cruft: `shelfDummy`, empty `seedForTests` on ChipClock. Tests: the chip calibration trio (thd, noise, bandwidth) is the best in the field and pins the ElectroSmash numbers, repitch and fm handle the write/read mod-phase issue, but the suite runs at 48 kHz / block 128 only and defers the rate matrix to 'Phase 6', so it would not catch its own block-size bug, a sample-rate scaling bug, or a NaN; no tap-timing test.

fatalFlaws: Block-size dependent character. 'Character (block rate, from `fsBase` at block start, one `log2`)' computes bits, `step`/`invStep`, `noiseAmp`, `bleedAmp` and the reconstruction targets once per host block. A 4096-sample block at 48 kHz gives 85 ms staircases in bit depth, noise floor and bleed level during a Time sweep, and `reconG/H` are 'ramped 5 ms' from those block-rate targets, so the reconstruction cutoff moves in 85 ms steps with 5 ms ramps on a big-buffer host and effectively per sample on a 32-sample host. The sound depends on block size, in the design whose stated angle is robustness. D0/D2's persistent 16-sample control countdown is the fix.

Its own noise scenario cannot pass and the plan's short-Time floor is missed by about 20 dB. `crust (a)` asserts 'same at Time 0 <= -80 dBFS', but with `kBitsAtMaxClock = 10` (step 2^-9), TPDF `0.5f * (rnd() + rnd())` (+-1 LSB, variance step^2/6) plus quantisation (step^2/12) the per-stage noise is about -60 dBFS at chip rate, white to 100 kHz, and the read 'output from the two newest chip samples (discarded intermediates carry only chip noise, since the input passed the 8.8 kHz MFB)' decimates by 4.17 with no chip-rate filter, so all of it folds into 0..24 kHz. After the 8 kHz recon pair and the weighted tap sum the Time-0 wet floor is about -67 to -70 dBFS at Decay 0. The same raw discard makes the floor sample-rate dependent (about 5 dB lower at 192 kHz, where nothing folds), and `srmatrix` cannot see it because it runs only scenarios #1 and #3.

Inconsistent implicit solve in a filter that is allowed negative damping. '`g`, `R2`, `h` recomputed at the 32-sample control tick, each ramped 5 ms; no per-sample tan/div' plus the admitted '**Ramped `h` is an approximation** while `g`/`R2` move'. h must equal 1/(1 + R2 g + g^2) at every sample for the TPT update to be the discretisation of anything; ramping the three independently while R2 < 0 (res > kResOscStart = 0.8) leaves the update outside the analysed stability region for 5 ms after every control tick, and the safety net is `kSvfStateClamp = 8`, a hard clamp, i.e. a click. Recompute the triple together at the control tick (D0/D2) and ramp nothing, or ramp only fc/res and recompute all three per sample. Whether the 32-sample tick is a persistent countdown or `i % 32` is not specified.

Same first-block glide as D0. The Multiplicative `fsSmooth` default-constructs to 1.0 (verified: JUCE initialises multiplicative smoothers to 1), and '`prepare` is idempotent: recompute coefficients, reset smoothers, `reset()`' snaps current to the previous target, so the first block after construction clamps to kFsChipAbsMin = 1 kHz and glides 17.6 octaves in 20 ms; no snap to the current Time anywhere.
scores.notes: The best inner-loop discipline of the three and the worst sound. Verified strengths: `p -= ticks` keeps the phase in [0,1); `u = (float) (1.0 - before) * c.invR; u += c.invR` is the correct tick timing; no transcendental per host sample (multiplicative smoother is one multiply, linear FM is one multiply, one division for invR); the tick loop is genuinely division- and modulo-free (`softCubic`, `roundToInt`, ternary wrap); the stored word is bounded without a clamp because softCubic's ceiling is exactly 1.0 and |noisy| <= 1.014 so roundToInt never overflows; quantised memory can never denormal; noise generated inside tick() is sample-rate invariant by construction; per-sample input sanitiser `if (! (abs (x) < kInputCeiling)) x = 0` is the right first line of defence; oversize blocks are chunked; FTZ is inside the engine; the 'never ramp step/invStep separately (up to 1 dB gain wobble)' invariant is correct and worth writing into code; `kStageDetune` costs three phase accumulators but no extra division (invR times constants). Its ceilings 0.894/1.135 at kSatBias 0.12 and satNorm = 1/(1 - tanh^2 b) check out. Weaknesses beyond the fatal list: one `MfbLowpass mfb` for the whole loop instead of one per chip and no output MFB, so tap 1 is -3 dB near 4.5 kHz against the plan's 'flat to ~1 kHz'; no THD-versus-Time model at all (softCubic only); `crust (b)` LOCKS IN aliasing ('alias at 500 Hz (4000 - 3*1500) within [-9, 0] dB re 300') which is the 'harsh and digital' failure the emulation must avoid; `absorbGain` before the saturator takes up to 18 dB off the feedback so Absorb 1 kills Decay; `kBleedPostRecon = false` filters the tick into a thump; `fm` picks 80 Hz without deriving it from D; no `isfinite` backstop for anything that goes non-finite internally; taking the plan's 10->6 bits literally puts the Time-1 wet floor near -40 dBFS which recirculates into a roar at Decay 0.9. Tests: `srmatrix` (44.1/96/192 kHz x blocks 1/17/4096), `coredelay` ((1835+1)/4 + recon delay = 461 +- 2 samples), `nan`, `flush`, and the smear envelope-stretch metric (30 ms burst emerges as 62 +- 10 ms at half pitch) are exactly what my lens wants and must be grafted; but the suite asserts a floor it cannot reach and a fold it should not want, and its rate matrix omits the one measurement (Time-0 floor) that is rate dependent.

fatalFlaws: No non-finite containment anywhere. 'Every node has a hard bound with no `jlimit` in the signal path' bounds amplitude only. A single NaN or inf host sample enters `loopIn = in[i] + feedback`, then `x = mfbOnePole(x_host); x = mfbBiquad(x)` BEFORE `chipClip`, so the MFB states, guard poles, ring, recon poles, LoopFilter ic1/ic2, Absorb lp, DC blocker, `feedback` and `ember` (published to the UI) all hold NaN until Clear or prepare; `std::tanh(NaN)` is NaN so nothing downstream recovers. Graft D1's per-sample `if (!(std::abs (x) < kInputCeiling)) x = 0` at the sum node and D0's per-block `isfinite(feedback)` -> reset() backstop.

Cross-thread state outside the atomic mailboxes. `void snapTimeOnNextBlock() { snapTime = true; }` writes the plain `bool clearing = false, snapTime = true;` from `applyExtraState` on the message thread while process() reads it; and `double getDelaySeconds() const; // for the readout / synced clamp display` has the editor read engine-owned float state directly. CLAUDE.md: UI->engine through lock-free atomic mailboxes, engine->UI through atomics the editor polls. One-word fixes (std::atomic<bool> or a command counter like requestClear; an atomic uiDelaySeconds as D0 publishes), but as written both are data races.

Sample-rate scaling of the hiss is inverted. `float hissRateComp = 1.0f; // sqrt(48000 / sr): constant spectral density`. White noise of per-sample amplitude A through a one-pole at a fixed 6 kHz has output variance proportional to A^2 * fc / sr; constant density needs A proportional to sqrt(sr / 48000) (D0's `noiseSrScale`). As written the hiss is about 6 dB low at 96 kHz and 12 dB low at 192 kHz, and `srinvariance` cannot see it because it measures the Time-1 floor where quantisation noise dominates by about 12 dB. Separately, the Time-0 floor is rate dependent by about 4 to 6 dB because the two-slot read discards intermediate chip samples with no chip-rate filter before decimation (same as D1; D0's chip-rate DAC pole avoids it).

Block-size assumption in the engine. 'both sized for the worst case and re-sized only in `prepare`' for the mono scratch and the per-sample Time-mod buffer, with no chunking path when a host delivers more than maxBlockSize samples (D0 and D1 both chunk). Hosts do exceed the prepared size; as written this is a buffer overrun waiting for the wrong host.
scores.notes: The best product and the best test suite, let down by containment and threading holes that D0 and D1 each closed. Verified for my lens: persistent `controlCountdown` members in BOTH ChipClock and TimeFilterLoop, so `cutoffSmooth.skip(16)` and the curve refresh are block-size independent (the thing D0 got wrong); the `nextWriteTime` float accumulator stays in [0, chipPeriod) with an exact `-= 1.0f` below 2^24 and never drifts unboundedly; after the write loop 'now' sits at chip time (writeIdx - 1) + frac with frac = 1 - nextWriteTime * ratio in (0, 1], reading slots writeIdx+1 / writeIdx+2 yields a constant N - 2 chip samples of delay and never touches a slot written this host sample even at 10 writes per sample (kFsChipCeil 400 kHz at 44.1 kHz); `reset(time01)` snaps the clock on the first block and preset load, so it is the only design without the start-up chirp; `ScopedNoDenormals` is inside process() so EngineTest gets FTZ; clearFade multiplies both out and feedback; ember = max(|y|, ember * release) is block-size independent; every node has a stated ceiling (chipClip 1.0, ic1 1.5 via `kSvfSatLevel * tanh(...)`, saturator 0.87/1.175, feedback 1.35 turned back into 1.0) and bounding ic1 does bound ic2 because s2's own recursion has |1 - 2 g^2 a1| < 1. Costs: one exp2f + one division per host sample (same as D0), two `% N` per stage per sample (trivial, but a carried readIdx with a branch is free), two std::tanh per sample. Weaknesses beyond the fatal list: no THD-versus-Time model (`chipClip` cubic gives H3/H1 = A^2/27 = 0.93 % at A 0.5 at every Time, 7x the plan's 0.13 % at 31 ms); the plan's fs_chip pulse train is dropped and the memory-wrap tick is admitted to be a hypothesis, then `crust` asserts it (4..24 peaks, 1.22 s spacing): a test protecting a guess; `handleClear`'s `if (c != clearCounter && !clearing)` never advances lastClearSeen during a fade so a press inside 8 ms schedules a redundant second clear (harmless); hand-rolled one-pole Time smoother instead of SmoothedValue (style, and one-pole never lands exactly); `kFilterMinHz = 150` is a recon/guard floor that never binds and clashes with the Filter parameter's 20 Hz; `kAbsorbFeedbackShare = 1.0` default cuts feedback 18 dB at Absorb 1 (D0's 4 dB split is the better default); '300 Hz sine transmits within 6 dB' has about 0.7 dB of margin; `smear` window [t0+0.07, t0+0.11] ends within a few ms of tap 1 draining. Tests missing for my lens: block-size matrix, NaN injection, THD, bare-core delay; `srinvariance` checks rates but not block sizes and measures the wrong floor.

graft: From D2: a persistent `controlCountdown` member in TimeFilterLoop, decremented per sample across block boundaries, with `skip (kCtrlInterval)` called only when it fires; delete `if (i % kCtrlInterval == 0)`. Add a `blockmatrix` scenario: the same 2 s Filter sweep at Decay 0.9 rendered at block sizes 1, 17, 128, 4096 with the same seed must be bit-identical (max |a - b| == 0.0), which is the only assertion that proves nothing in the loop depends on block size.

From D1: wrap the phase every sample (`p -= ticks` after the tick loop, `phase` in [0,1)), derive the tick offset as `u = (1 - before) * invRatio; u += invRatio`, and use the wrapped phase directly as readFrac. Delete `floor(phase) - floor(phaseBefore)` on an unbounded double.

From D2 plus the template: snap `logFsSmooth` with `setCurrentAndTargetValue` on the first block after every prepare (the template's `firstBlock` idiom, as ExampleEngine already does for its three smoothers), and provide `snapTimeOnNextBlock()` as a std::atomic<bool> or a command counter (never a plain bool) called from applyExtraState and preset load. Sync division changes keep smearing per the plan.

From D1 and D0 together: per-sample `if (!(std::abs (x) < kInputCeiling)) x = 0` (kInputCeiling 1e4) at the loop sum node AND the per-block `isfinite(fb)` -> flushAll() backstop. Add D1's `nan` scenario extended to three injections (NaN, inf, 1e30 at sample 37 of a 128 block): every output sample after that block finite, and the loop back within 1 dB of its pre-injection RMS within 1 s.

From D1: the `srmatrix` scenario, but run on the measurements that can actually move: Time-0 wet noise floor (dBFS), Time-1 floor, `threestep` echo time, `thd` at Time01 0.0244, smear pitch ratio, runaway RMS, at 44.1 / 48 / 96 / 192 kHz x blocks 1 / 17 / 128 / 4096, tolerances +-1 dB / +-1 % / +-2 dB, no NaN. D0's chip-rate DAC pole should pass the Time-0 floor row; D1/D2's raw discard would miss it by 4 to 6 dB. That row is the number that decides whether the synthesis keeps the DAC pole.

From D1: the `coredelay` bare-stage impulse test: one PTStage driven by ChipClock at a snapped Time with modOct 0, BITS 24, noise and bleed 0; the impulse peak must land at kStageWords / ratio + filter group delay +-2 host samples at 48 kHz and at the same chip-sample count at 96 kHz.

From D2: `uiLoopEnergy` as peak |y| with a 50 ms release (block-size independent; D0's sqrt(energy / n) is per-sample |y| at block 1 and 85 ms RMS at 4096). Keep D0's atomic `uiDelaySeconds`; never a cross-thread getter.

From D2, with D0's scaling: inject the analog hiss AFTER the reconstruction filter through a fixed 6 kHz one-pole (D0's pre-recon hiss is a sub-700 Hz rumble at Time 1), with amplitude proportional to sqrt(sr / 48000) (D0's `noiseSrScale`; D2's `sqrt(48000 / sr)` is inverted).

From D2: replace D0's bool `kWriteAntiAlias` one-pole with a compile-time `kGuardPoles` 0/1/2 tracking write filter at min(0.45 fs_chip, 8 kHz) using the `aAA` coefficient D0 already computes at control rate, and print the folded alias level (3.3 kHz -> 300 Hz at Time 1) in the crust scenario.

From D2: keep D0's `y *= clearGain` placement (it fades wet and feedback together) but raise CLEAR_FADE_SEC from 0.003 to 0.005..0.008, and use D2's relative `clear` criterion (largest sample-to-sample step during the fade <= 1.5x the largest step in the preceding 200 ms) instead of D0's absolute 0.05, which is frequency dependent.

From D2: the test pieces `threestep` (energy peaks at D/3, 2D/3, D +-3 ms, tap ratios 0.8 +-0.15, later taps darker by hfFraction, single peak with DYBBUK_PT_STAGES=1), `nonidentical` with the exact-zero seeded control and differing-fraction >= 0.5, `sidebands` grid-vs-half-grid with fMod derived from getDelaySeconds()-style measured D, and `runaway` at Decay 0.95 / 1.0 / 1.15 plus the worst case (Time Mod depth 1 at ~173 Hz, Res 0.95, Filter 20 Hz); every expectation written against delaySecondsForTime01() so retuning kMemoryWords moves them.

From D1: the smear envelope-stretch metric (30 ms burst at 0.3 with Time halved during the delay must emerge as a 62 +-10 ms event at half pitch, min 5 ms RMS inside the span > 0.4 of max, no dropout) added to D0's `repitch`; it is the sharpest crossfade detector of the three suites.

From D2: the `DYBBUK_PT_STAGES` CMake define for the 1-vs-3 A/B, and the 'struct defaults are for the harness; APVTS defaults are the user's' note on TimeFilterLoop::Params (CLAUDE.md 'Defaults belong to the user').
From D1 (and D2): `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` at the top of DybbukEngine::process so EngineTest gets FTZ; the processor's copy stays.

From D1's cost discipline, applied to D0's code so its claims become true: cache `h = 1 / (1 + g*(g + k))` in TptSvf::setG/setK (D2 caches a1/a2/a3 at control rate) to remove ten per-sample divisions; turn `(ax - CLIP_KNEE) / (1 - CLIP_KNEE)` into a constexpr multiply; keep the Pade division in the tick but document 'one division per tick'; add a debug assert `nTicks <= kMaxTicksPerHostSample` with kMaxTicksPerHostSample = (int) std::ceil (FS_CHIP_HARD_MAX / 44100.0) + 1 = 7.

From D1: write the invariant into code: `step` and `invStep` are recomputed as a pair at control rate and never ramped independently (ramping them apart gives up to 1 dB gain wobble). D0 already obeys it; the comment is what stops a future 'smooth everything' edit.
From D0/D1 into whatever D2 surface is kept: chunk any host block larger than maxBlock (`for (int start = 0; start < n; start += maxBlock)`) so the scratch and Time-mod buffers can never overrun.

Optional, from D1: `kStageDetune {1.0, 1.012, 0.991}` implemented as per-stage phase accumulators fed `ratio * detune[s]` and `invRatio * invDetune[s]` (constants, no extra division). Ship {1, 1, 1} as the default so D0's single shared Frame stays the hot path; enable only if the listening A/B asks for tap chorus.
unresolved: Chip-rate anti-alias before the read (D0's DAC one-pole at min(0.45 fs_chip, 8 kHz), run per tick) versus raw discard of intermediate chip samples (D1, D2). It decides both whether the plan's -90 dBFS short-Time floor is reachable and whether the floor is sample-rate invariant (D1/D2 drift 4 to 6 dB between 48 and 192 kHz). Only the srmatrix Time-0 floor row settles it; nobody has run it.

Per-sample cost contract. D0 and D2 spend one exp/exp2 plus one division per host sample; D1 spends one multiply plus one division (multiplicative smoother, linear FM). The plan's risk 3 ('precompute ratio increments per block') is impossible with per-sample log-domain FM, so the FM law (exponential octaves vs linear clock ratio) is simultaneously a musical question and the per-sample budget. Decide with a profile at 192 kHz / 4096 blocks / full FM depth, not by assertion.

Control-rate stepping under deep audio-rate FM: step/invStep, aDac, recG and the guard coefficient move in 16-sample steps while the phase increment moves per sample. At +-3 octaves and 1 kHz mod that is a 3 kHz staircase on the quantiser LSB and on two tracking filters; nobody measured whether it is audible. A sideband-spectrum comparison at kCtrlInterval 16 vs 4 is needed before the constant is fixed.

Ticks-per-host-sample ceiling at 44.1 kHz with FM headroom: D0's FS_CHIP_HARD_MAX 250 kHz gives 6 to 7 ticks, D2's kFsChipCeil 400 kHz gives 9 to 10, each tick carrying two PRNG calls and (in D0) a Pade division. The ceiling should be chosen against a measured worst-case CPU figure with three stages, not a guess; it also bounds the write-loop iteration count that makes the per-sample cost data dependent.

NaN policy beyond containment: per-sample zeroing (D1) hides a host fault silently, per-block flush (D0) lets up to one block of NaN out before recovering. The synthesis should do both; whether to also publish a fault flag atomic to the UI (so the user learns why the loop just emptied) is open.

Preset load: snap Time (D2) or smear it like a knob (D0/D1 by omission). The plan requires Sync division changes to smear and is silent on preset loads; the snap also needs a thread-safe mailbox, which no design has fully specified.

Feedback topology, tap-sum (all three defaults) versus full-chain (D0's `kFeedbackFromTapSum = false`): not a real-time question, but it changes the comb the runaway limit cycle locks onto, so every runaway/clear bound in every suite is written against one topology only.

Absolute bit/noise calibration (10->6, 11->8, 12->7 bits, Time-0 floors from -70 to -89 dBFS, Time-1 floors from -40 to -61) and therefore the Time-1 roar at Decay >= 0.9; no design has a hardware measurement for the long end.

What the hardware 'ticking' physically is: fs_chip pulse train plus fs_chip/2 square (D0/D1, per plan) versus a memory-wrap click per stage delay (D2's admitted hypothesis, which its `crust` test enshrines). The synthesis should carry all three components behind separate dB constants under one kCrust trim so the listening pass can zero any of them.
